metadata.title: Vibecoders Welcome
metadata.purpose: Show non-coders the two legitimate uses of Claude Code (mockup for devs, personal tool for yourself), the seven-step setup, DESIGN.md for brand styling, and the four situations where you should use something else instead.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

beats.narration_text: Bonjour. This is Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude: can I actually build something with Claude Code if I don't know how to code? Here's what that looks like — because vibecoding is real, it's useful, and you don't write a single line.

props.ask: Can I actually build something with Claude Code if I don't know how to code?
props.answer_preview: Yes. Two use cases worth your time, and a 7-step setup…
props.command: Someone asked Claude: can I actually build something with Claude Code if I don't know how to code?

beats.narration_text: Two use cases that actually hold up. One: build a clickable mockup and hand it to a developer or designer so they stop guessing what you meant. Two: build a small personal tool — a dashboard, a custom tracker — that does a specific job better than a generic chat interface. Rough edges are fine because nobody else sees them.

illustration.concept: Two-lane split diagram on cream. Left lane: a hand-drawn arrow going from a rough sketch to a clickable web page icon, labeled 'Mockup for devs.' Right lane: a small dashboard icon with a single user figure, labeled 'Personal tool.' Each lane has a short sub-note. Terracotta accent on the lane separator line only.
illustration.layout: Two equal columns, terracotta vertical divider, minimal hand-drawn icons, labels in EB Garamond

beats.narration_text: Seven steps to get set up. One: download the app and get a paid plan. Two: create one clean empty folder on your computer — nothing private, nothing you'd hate to lose. Three: turn on bypass permissions in settings so Claude doesn't ask your approval for every edit. Four: connect Netlify and Supabase — both free for basic needs — so your site can go live. Five: select the folder you created. Six: pick your model. Seven: build.

illustration.concept: Seven numbered steps as a vertical staircase or numbered list, hand-drawn. Each step has a bold number, a 3-4 word action label, and a small icon (app icon, folder, toggle switch, two connector logos, folder select, model selector, build icon). Terracotta on step numbers only.
illustration.layout: Vertical numbered list, left-aligned, generous spacing, icons on the right of each step label

beats.narration_text: The fastest way to stop your site looking like every other AI-generated site: drop in a DESIGN.md file. It's a plain text file that spells out a full design system — exact colors, fonts, spacing. Drop it in your folder and tell Claude to use it for all styling. Sites like getdesign.md offer them free for dozens of well-known brands.

card.sub: Drop in a design system file. Claude follows it everywhere.

beats.narration_text: Tell Claude to use shadcn/ui components. That one line makes your buttons, forms, and menus look professionally built instead of homemade. It burns more tokens, so use it on projects where polish matters — dashboards, onboarding flows, anything with forms.

card.sub: One instruction. Professional components. Worth the token cost on real projects.

beats.narration_text: Claude Code is the wrong tool for plenty of things. Want a small widget you'll look at once — use an Artifact in a normal chat, no setup needed. Writing a document or a spreadsheet — use Cowork. Making a single image — go to ChatGPT. And the rule that stops most wasted sessions: don't take longer to build it than you'd spend using it. Performative productivity is still a trap.

illustration.concept: Decision tree or routing diagram on cream. Central question: 'What are you building?' Four branches with labeled outcomes: Widget / one-off → Artifact. Document / spreadsheet → Cowork. Single image → ChatGPT. Real app or tool → Code. Terracotta on the 'Real app or tool → Code' branch only.
illustration.layout: Central diamond decision node with four radiating branches, each ending in a tool label in a small rounded box

beats.narration_text: This week: find one boring job you do manually — extracting information from files, building a simple tracker, a landing page for something real — and give Claude Code thirty minutes. Start with a screenshot of something you like, describe the end result in one sentence, and react to what comes back. You do not need to know what code is. You just need a clear picture of what you want to exist.

card.sub: Screenshot + one sentence. React. Iterate. You don't need to touch code.

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. Vibecoders Welcome. Two use cases, seven steps, one design file, and four situations to skip it — that is the whole map.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want to use Claude Code but you're not a professional developer — you write code occasionally and mostly by feel. Ask Claude to show you the three Claude Code habits that matter most for non-professionals: how to scope a session, how to know when to stop and verify, and what to do when the code looks right but you're not sure.
